description: Derived controlled-language dictionary for the LAAS software-documentation profile: the markdown tables in software-docs.md section 3 are authoritative, each term carries exactly one approved meaning and one part of speech (STE-C-04), no term appears in both the nouns list and the verbs list, and entries in forbidden with class 'notation' are blocking at every Consequence Tier, including CT0 (software-docs.md section 5.2, deviation).

nouns.meaning: The identifier of one published interface contract, stated as a version string and a named scheme.
A change that makes a previously documented caller stop working without a change by that caller.
The output file set produced by one documentation build, identified by a build identifier.
The unique identifier of one documentation build run.
The one URL that a published page declares as its own address for indexing.
The record of one shipped change, bound to one version string.
A block of code or commands in a page that a reader is expected to run.
A literal string the software parses: a symbol name, a command, a flag, a path, or an environment variable name.
The content hash that identifies one commit in the source repository.
The value a documented parameter takes when the caller supplies none.
A published statement that names a feature, the version that deprecated it, and the version or date that removes it.
One published web location that serves pages to a stated audience.
A content delivery network store that serves a copy of a published page after the origin changes.
The stated date after which a named version receives no further support.
A named runtime value read by the software, written verbatim as a code identifier.
The integer a command returns to its caller on completion.
A named runtime switch that enables or disables a behaviour without a code change.
A documentation site reachable only by members of the publishing organization.
A published procedure that moves a reader's system from one named version to another named version.
A documentation site reachable by any reader on the internet.
One page that has reached a documentation site and can be fetched by a reader of that site.
One of drafted, merged, built, published, cached, withdrawn.
A placeholder written in place of a secret value, marked as a placeholder.
A published mapping from one URL to another URL, served to every request for the first URL.
The customer-facing description of the changes in one named version.
The named program and version that executes a code example.
A version string of the form MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH under Semantic Versioning.
The file, test, or schema that proves a documented behaviour, cited by path and line.
A documentation site reachable only by the publishing team, used before a public publish.
A published claim that a named component works with a named component from a named version.
The ordered sequence of versions a reader must pass through to reach a target version.
The complete literal designator of one release, written verbatim with its named scheme.

verbs.meaning: Record a named party's decision to permit an action.
Prevent an action from proceeding, with the reason recorded.
Produce a build artifact from source files by running a named build command.
Name the source of record for a stated behaviour, by path and line.
Publish a deprecation notice that names the deprecating version and the removal version or date.
Run a code example on a named runtime and record the exit status.
Instruct an edge cache to discard its stored copy of a named URL.
Combine a change into the default branch of the source repository.
Fix a dependency or an example to one named version string.
Make a page fetchable by readers of a named documentation site.
Replace a secret value with a marked placeholder before publication.
Serve requests for one URL from another URL by a published redirect rule.
Return a named file to a named prior state in the source repository.
Restore a file to a prior commit. The published copy is unaffected.
Read a change against stated criteria and record the findings.
Replace a disclosed secret with a new secret value.
Compare a claim against an independent source and record the result.
Remove a published page from a documentation site and record the removal.

forbidden.reason: A revert restores a file to a prior commit. It does not recall a published page from a reader, a cache, or a crawler (STE-SWD-03).
forbidden.replacement: revert only for the repository; withdraw for the page; state page reversibility separately

forbidden.reason: No named publication target and no stated reach, so the scope axis is unassessable (STE-SWD-04).
forbidden.replacement: publish to the staging, internal, or public site

forbidden.reason: Resolves to a different value on a different day than the day the record is read (STE-SWD-02).
forbidden.replacement: the version string and its named scheme

forbidden.reason: Collides with the semver level and with the consequence enum at conformance/laas/data.json.
forbidden.replacement: the semver level, or the enum value, or the stated number

forbidden.reason: Asserts the step is easy and suppresses the failure case.
forbidden.replacement: the step, and its expected observable result

forbidden.reason: States a hope, not an executed result (ste-core.md section 3.2).
forbidden.replacement: the exit status, the runtime, and the date of execution, or not executed

forbidden.reason: Self-assessed performance with no measurement basis (STE-SWD-11).
forbidden.replacement: the number, the unit, the measurement basis, and the date

forbidden.reason: Reads as a contractual promise of unbounded scope.
Gives the reader no date and no version to plan against.
forbidden.replacement: deprecated in <version>, removed in <version or date>

forbidden.reason: Hides a breaking change behind a size adjective (STE-SWD-09).
forbidden.replacement: breaking change, the affected interface, and the required reader action
the actor_id or the named component

forbidden.reason: Claims a value is synthetic without evidence. A real key has shipped this way (STE-SWD-10).
forbidden.replacement: redacted credential, with the redaction stated

forbidden.reason: Implies restoration of reader state, which no publication control provides.
forbidden.replacement: withdraw the published page, then state what readers already ran

forbidden.term: etc. (in a flag or parameter list)
forbidden.reason: Unbounded scope in a list a reader will execute against (STE-SWD-01).
forbidden.replacement: the complete list, or the count and the selection rule
